expected_behavior: A receipt declaring claim_kind 'phantom_kind_v99', which gate_registry.json does not define, must refuse/park nonzero (unclassified -> INSUFFICIENT_DEPTH exit 3, or REJECTED exit 1 if a tier also fails) and never default to VERIFIED exit 0.
actual_behavior: claim_verify parked the isolated receipt as INSUFFICIENT_DEPTH exit 3 purely on the unclassified claim_kind (tier0 PASS, tiers 1-4 SKIP, required_unmet empty — the unclassified flag alone blocked VERIFIED); the companion corpus-marked receipt was REJECTED exit 1 at tier0 (classification 'hostile_control_fixture' not in claimgate.py's allowed set), which masks the class behind an unrelated failure and is why the isolated variant is the load-bearing probe.

_notes.fixture_roles: stale_policy_receipt_isolated.json = the load-bearing regression tripwire (only defect is the phantom claim_kind; if it ever exits 0 the stale_policy hole has opened). stale_policy_receipt.json = corpus-marked variant per the hostile-corpus classification rule; exits 1 at tier0 so it cannot isolate this class. stale_policy_pinned_registry.json = verbatim pinned copy of the policy in force at authoring time (sha256 a346040d3a30d7c6dfa0586da963492b61d349b6c96f4ef4d05e91b0b1040052) proving phantom_kind_v99 was policy-undefined, not later-removed.
_notes.mechanism: claim_verify.py: reg['claim_kinds'].get(claim_kind) -> None sets unclassified=True and falls back to required={'tier0'}; final dispatch routes unclassified to INSUFFICIENT_DEPTH exit 3 even when every required tier passed and nothing failed. Fail-closed as designed.
_notes.classification_deviation: The corpus rule mandates classification 'hostile_control_fixture' inside fixtures; on the isolated receipt that token would trip tier0 R1 (classification_not_allowed) and hide the stale_policy path behind an unrelated rejection, so it carries an allowed token plus hostile_control_fixture:true and promotion_allowed:false under the rule's 'where JSON shape allows' clause. The marked companion honors the rule literally.
